name: Cardiac Surgery, CABG Indications, Valve Procedures, and Cardiopulmonary Bypass
hyTerms: contact activation of clotting and complement

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Kirklin/Barratt-Boyes Cardiac Surgery 4th ed
clinicalPearls: CABG is indicated for left main stenosis >= 50%, triple-vessel CAD, or multivessel CAD in diabetic patients
LIMA anastomosed to the LAD is the premier conduit, delivering > 90% ten-year patency and survival benefit
Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis (valve area < 1.0 cm2, mean gradient > 40 mmHg) mandates prompt valve replacement
Cardiopulmonary bypass requires systemic heparinization targeting activated clotting time (ACT) > 480 seconds
Mitral valve repair with an annuloplasty ring achieves superior survival compared to replacement for primary MR
reference.pathophysiology: Coronary atherosclerosis induces chronic myocardial ischemia and anginal symptoms through progressive luminal compromise. Valvular stenosis produces progressive pressure overload, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction, while regurgitation produces volume overload and eccentric chamber remodeling. Cardiopulmonary bypass triggers systemic inflammatory cascades via contact activation of clotting and complement pathways.
additionalDifferentials: Acute aortic dissection with coronary ostial involvement
Severe secondary functional mitral regurgitation from ischemic cardiomyopathy
additionalInvestigations: Coronary angiography with calculation of anatomical SYNTAX score
Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography for valve area and ventricular function
Carotid duplex ultrasound to assess cerebrovascular disease prior to bypass
